title: Emergence, Not Bandwidth: Physical Coupling and the Limits of Learned Multi-Agent Communication
abstract: arXiv:2609.34373v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Rate-limited multi-agent teams raise three questions the emergent-communication literature has answered only empirically: what an optimal message should encode, what compression costs over a horizon, and when a learned protocol is unique enough for a teammate to read. We answer them for rate-limited Dec-POMDPs, then measure how far reinforcement learning falls short of the optimum. Our theorems fix what is achievable independently of any learner, so a gap between an engineered and a learned sender at the same bit budget is an optimization fact, not an information-theoretic one. We instantiate this on three MuJoCo arenas spanning zero, partial and rigid physical coupling, charging every condition exactly 2 bits per decision, and create the discriminating regime by closing a physical side channel within one arena, holding bodies, task and reward fixed. translated_title: 涌现而非带宽：物理耦合与学习型多智能体通信的极限
translated_abstract: 速率受限的多智能体团队提出了三个涌现通信文献此前仅从经验上回答过的问题：最优消息应当编码什么内容、压缩在决策跨度上的代价是多少，以及学习到的协议何时足够独特以使队友能够解读。我们针对速率受限的Dec-POMDP回答了这些问题，进而衡量强化学习与最优解之间的差距。我们的定理独立于任何学习器确定了可达到的性能上限，因此在相同比特预算下，工程设计的发送者与学习得到的发送者之间的差距是一个优化问题，而非信息论问题。我们在三个MuJoCo竞技场上进行实例化验证，涵盖零耦合、部分耦合和刚性物理耦合三种情形，对每种条件精确收取每决策2比特的通信费用，并通过在其中一个竞技场内关闭物理侧信道来构造具有区分力的实验条件，同时保持智能体身体、任务和奖励不变。通信价值由耦合程度决定：在通过共享……的刚性耦合下……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文首次为速率受限的Dec-POMDP建立了最优通信的理论刻画，证明通信的价值由智能体间的物理耦合程度而非带宽决定，并通过MuJoCo实验表明学习到的通信协议与理论最优协议之间的差距源于优化不足而非信息论限制。
en_tdlr: This paper provides the first theoretical characterization of optimal communication for rate-limited Dec-POMDPs, proving that communication value is governed by physical coupling between agents rather than bandwidth, and demonstrating through MuJoCo experiments that the gap between learned and optimal protocols stems from optimization failure rather than information-theoretic limits.
